meaning_en: as for; marks the topic of the sentence

examples.japanese: 私は学生です。
examples.english: I am a student.

examples.japanese: 今日は天気がいいです。
examples.english: The weather is nice today.

examples.japanese: この本はおもしろいです。
examples.english: This book is interesting.

notes: Written は but pronounced 'wa'. It sets up what the sentence is about; the key information comes after it.

meaning_en: marks the subject; points out new or focused information

examples.japanese: 雨が降っています。
examples.english: It is raining.

examples.japanese: だれが窓を開けましたか。
examples.english: Who opened the window?

examples.japanese: 私が行きます。
examples.english: I'll be the one to go.

notes: Question words such as だれ and 何 take が, never は, when they are the subject. が is also used with 好き, ほしい, 上手 and わかる for the thing liked, wanted or understood.

meaning_en: marks the direct object of a verb; marks a place moved through or left

examples.japanese: 毎朝パンを食べます。
examples.english: I eat bread every morning.

examples.japanese: 姉は新しいかばんを買いました。
examples.english: My older sister bought a new bag.

examples.japanese: 公園を散歩しました。
examples.english: I took a walk in the park.

notes: Written を but pronounced 'o'. With movement verbs such as 歩く, 散歩する and 出る it marks the route or the place being left.

meaning_en: at; on; in (a specific point in time)

examples.japanese: 毎朝7時に起きます。
examples.english: I get up at seven every morning.

examples.japanese: 日曜日に友達と会います。
examples.english: I'm meeting a friend on Sunday.

examples.japanese: 8月に国へ帰ります。
examples.english: I'm going back to my country in August.

notes: Used with clock times, dates, days of the week and months. Relative words such as 今日, 明日, 毎日 and 来週 take no に.

meaning_en: to; into (the destination of movement)
formation: Noun + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る

examples.japanese: 毎日バスで学校に行きます。
examples.english: I go to school by bus every day.

examples.japanese: 夜10時に家に帰りました。
examples.english: I got home at 10 p.m.

examples.japanese: 来月、姉が日本に来ます。
examples.english: My older sister is coming to Japan next month.

notes: Close in meaning to へ. に puts the focus on the arrival point, へ on the direction.

meaning_en: in; at; on (where someone or something is)
formation: Noun + に + ある / いる

examples.japanese: 机の上に辞書があります。
examples.english: There is a dictionary on the desk.

examples.japanese: 姉は東京に住んでいます。
examples.english: My older sister lives in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 猫は今どこにいますか。
examples.english: Where is the cat now?

notes: Used with ある, いる and 住む. For the place where an action happens (eat, study, play), use で instead.

meaning_en: to (the person who receives or is the target of an action)

examples.japanese: 母に手紙を書きます。
examples.english: I'm going to write a letter to my mother.

examples.japanese: 妹に本を貸しました。
examples.english: I lent a book to my younger sister.

examples.japanese: 友達に電話をかけました。
examples.english: I called my friend.

notes: Common with あげる, 貸す, 教える, 見せる, 電話をかける and 会う. With もらう and 借りる, に marks the person you get something from.

meaning_en: per; in (how many times within a period)

examples.japanese: 一週間に二回、プールで泳ぎます。
examples.english: I swim in the pool twice a week.

examples.japanese: 母は一日に二回、犬の散歩をします。
examples.english: My mother walks the dog twice a day.

examples.japanese: 一年に一度、家族で旅行します。
examples.english: Once a year, my family goes on a trip.

notes: The period comes first, then に, then the number of times: 月に一回 (once a month).

meaning_en: to; toward (the direction of movement)

examples.japanese: 夏休みに北海道へ行きます。
examples.english: I'm going to Hokkaido during summer vacation.

examples.japanese: 来週、国へ帰ります。
examples.english: I'm going back to my home country next week.

examples.japanese: どこへ行きますか。
examples.english: Where are you going?

notes: Written へ but pronounced 'e'. Usually interchangeable with に for destinations; へ stresses the direction a little more.

meaning_en: at; in (the place where an action happens)

examples.japanese: 図書館で本を読みます。
examples.english: I read books at the library.

examples.japanese: きのう、デパートでくつを買いました。
examples.english: Yesterday I bought shoes at the department store.

examples.japanese: 駅の前で友達を待ちました。
examples.english: I waited for my friend in front of the station.

notes: Compare 教室にいます (being somewhere: に) with 教室で勉強します (doing something there: で).

pattern: あげる / くれる / もらう
meaning_en: give (to someone else); give (to me or my group); receive
formation: Noun (receiver) + に + Noun + を + あげる / Noun (giver) + が + Noun + を + くれる / Noun (giver) + に + Noun + を + もらう

examples.japanese: 私は弟に古いゲームをあげた。
examples.english: I gave my old game to my little brother.

examples.japanese: 姉が誕生日にかわいいかばんをくれました。
examples.english: My older sister gave me a cute bag for my birthday.

examples.japanese: 友達から旅行のおみやげをもらった。
examples.english: I got a souvenir from my friend's trip.

notes: くれる is used only when the receiver is the speaker or someone in the speaker's group. With もらう the giver can be marked with に or から.

meaning_en: do something for someone (as a favor)

examples.japanese: 妹の宿題を手伝ってあげました。
examples.english: I helped my little sister with her homework.

examples.japanese: 道に迷っている人に、駅までの行き方を教えてあげた。
examples.english: I showed someone who was lost how to get to the station.

examples.japanese: 重そうだね。持ってあげようか。
examples.english: That looks heavy. Want me to carry it for you?

notes: Said directly to a superior it can sound condescending; use the humble お〜しましょうか (お持ちしましょうか) instead.

meaning_en: someone does something for me (or my group)

examples.japanese: 友達が引っ越しを手伝ってくれた。
examples.english: A friend helped me move.

examples.japanese: 父が駅まで車で送ってくれました。
examples.english: My father drove me to the station.

examples.japanese: 母が毎朝お弁当を作ってくれます。
examples.english: My mother makes me a boxed lunch every morning.

notes: The subject is the person doing the favor; the one who benefits is the speaker or someone close to them.

meaning_en: have someone do something (for me); get someone to do

examples.japanese: 先輩にレポートを見てもらった。
examples.english: I had a senior student look over my report.

examples.japanese: 友達に写真を撮ってもらった。
examples.english: I had a friend take my picture.

examples.japanese: 分からないところを先生に説明してもらいました。
examples.english: I had the teacher explain the parts I didn't understand.

notes: The receiver of the favor is the subject, and the person who does the action is marked with に.

meaning_en: (honorific) someone kindly does for me; (humble) I receive the favor of someone doing
formation: Verb-te + くださる / Verb-te + いただく

examples.japanese: 先生が私の作文を直してくださいました。
examples.english: My teacher kindly corrected my essay.

examples.japanese: ホテルの方に、おいしい店を教えていただきました。
examples.english: The hotel staff kindly told me about a good restaurant.

examples.japanese: 今日は来ていただいて、ありがとうございました。
examples.english: Thank you very much for coming today.

notes: くださる is the honorific version of くれる (ます-form: くださいます); いただく is the humble version of もらう.

meaning_en: do something and go; go on doing (from now into the future)

examples.japanese: 雨が降りそうだから、傘を持っていきます。
examples.english: It looks like rain, so I'll take an umbrella.

examples.japanese: これからもっと寒くなっていくでしょう。
examples.english: It will probably keep getting colder from now on.

examples.japanese: 時間があるなら、お茶を飲んでいきませんか。
examples.english: If you have time, won't you have some tea before you go?

notes: Movement or change away from the speaker, or from now toward the future. Compare 〜てくる.

meaning_en: do something and come back; come doing; (change) up to now; start to

examples.japanese: ちょっとコンビニに行ってきます。
examples.english: I'm just popping out to the convenience store.

examples.japanese: 日本語が少しずつ分かってきた。
examples.english: I've gradually started to understand Japanese.

examples.japanese: おなかがすいてきた。
examples.english: I'm starting to get hungry.

notes: Movement or change toward the speaker, or from the past up to now. 行ってきます literally means 'I'll go and come back.'

meaning_en: finish completely; do by accident; end up doing (with regret)

examples.japanese: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I left my umbrella on the train.

examples.japanese: この本はおもしろくて、一晩で読んでしまった。
examples.english: This book was so interesting that I read the whole thing in one night.

examples.japanese: あ、ケーキを全部食べちゃった。
examples.english: Oops, I ate all the cake.

notes: In speech 〜てしまう contracts to 〜ちゃう, and 〜でしまう to 〜じゃう (飲んじゃう).

meaning_en: do in advance (to prepare); do and leave as is

examples.japanese: 旅行の前に、ホテルを予約しておきます。
examples.english: I'll book the hotel before the trip.

examples.japanese: パーティーのために、飲み物を冷やしておいた。
examples.english: I chilled the drinks for the party.

examples.japanese: エアコンはつけておいてください。
examples.english: Please leave the air conditioner on.

notes: In casual speech 〜ておく often becomes 〜とく (買っとく), and 〜でおく becomes 〜どく (読んどく).

meaning_en: try doing (to see what it is like)

examples.japanese: このシャツ、着てみてもいいですか。
examples.english: May I try this shirt on?

examples.japanese: 新しくできたラーメン屋に行ってみた。
examples.english: I went to check out the new ramen shop.

examples.japanese: 日本の料理を自分で作ってみたいです。
examples.english: I want to try making Japanese food myself.

notes: Means trying something out to see the result, not making an effort to do something difficult.
